title: Russia's Ruble during the onset of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in early 2022: The role of implied volatility and attention

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors model intraday price fluctuations of the USD/RUB and EUR/RUB exchange rates using high-frequency realized variance calculated from 5-minute trading prices divided into six 4-hour trading windows. To predict future price variations, they build autoregressive volatility models (similar to HAR models) estimated via OLS. The models incorporate intraday seasonality dummies, war-onset day effects, high-frequency Google search volume indices as attention proxies, and intraday implied volatilities extracted directly from Bloomberg OTC currency options.
extraction.data_period: 1st of December 2021 to 7th of March 2022, 5-minute intraday
extraction.universe: USD/RUB and EUR/RUB foreign exchange markets and at-the-money monthly currency options
key_findings: Both high-frequency investor attention (Google searches) and implied volatility are useful for predicting intraday price fluctuations of the USD/RUB and EUR/RUB exchange rates.
Implied volatility encompasses intraday attention measures when both are included in the model, providing superior model fit and rendering attention variables statistically insignificant.
Intraday volatility exhibits clear non-linear seasonality across trading windows during 24-hour weekday trading.
Changes in investors' expectations are more relevant for the EUR/RUB exchange rate than USD/RUB, reflecting Europe's tighter economic ties and geographic proximity to the conflict.
limitations: Google search volume indices can be noisy in the short term and their timely implementation is challenging as search terms are not known in advance.
Implied volatilities tend to be biased upwards, which may be amplified during sudden crisis periods when information unfolds continuously.
